subject: microbiology
title: Complement Pathways II: Lectin Pathway, Membrane Attack Complex and C1 Esterase Inhibitor

steps.tx: The **lectin pathway** starts without antibody or tick over: mannose binding lectin (MBL) and ficolins read microbial mannose and acetyl patterns, their associated proteases (MASP1 and 2) cleave C4 and C2, and the same C4b2a convertase as classical results. It is pattern recognition written in complement protein, innate immunity's third door into one cascade.
steps.say: MBL reads mannose where C1q reads antibody; both build the same convertase.

left.title: Lectin initiation
points: MBL and ficolins bind microbial sugars
MASP proteases activate C4 and C2
No antibody required
Collectin family shares collagenous structure with C1q

right.title: Lectin deficiency
points: MBL variants common in populations
Childhood infection susceptibility debated by severity
Compounding with other immune defects matters
Replacement not standard practice

steps.tx: All pathways converge at **C3 convertase** and multiply through the amplification loop, then C5 convertases (C4b2a3b, C3bBb3b) split C5, launching terminal assembly. Convergence explains why C3 deficiency devastates every route and why laboratory patterns (C4 low or normal) localise which door burned.
steps.say: Three doors, one C3 hallway; C4 tells you whether the classical or lectin door was used.

steps.tx: The **membrane attack complex** (C5b with C6, C7, C8 and polymerised C9) punches 10 nanometre pores into gram negative membranes, lysing Neisseria efficiently and most gram positives not at all (thick peptidoglycan shields), which is why terminal deficiency selects Neisseria alone among common pathogens. Sublytic MAC on host cells signals and inflames instead of killing.
steps.say: MAC drills gram negative envelopes; thick gram positive walls shrug it off.

left.title: MAC assembly
points: C5b anchors, C6 C7 insert membrane
C8 begins pore, C9 polymerises (10 to 18 units)
Gram negative lysis, Neisseria exquisitely
CD59 (protectin) blocks C9 on self

right.title: MAC pathology
points: Sublytic MAC activates endothelium and platelets
PNH: CD59 absent, MAC lyses own red cells
Terminal deficiency: recurrent meningococcal disease
Soluble MAC marks complement activation in TMA

steps.tx: **C1 esterase inhibitor** (C1 INH) restrains C1r and C1s, MASPs, kallikrein and factor XIIa, so its deficiency unleashes bradykinin (hereditary angioedema: recurrent non itchy swelling, laryngeal attacks, abdominal pain, low C4, normal C1q in hereditary forms), treated by C1 INH concentrates, bradykinin receptor blockade (icatibant) and kallikrein inhibitors, never relying on antihistamines or steroids.
steps.say: Bradykinin swelling ignores antihistamines; replace the inhibitor or block its pathway.

left.title: HAE portrait
points: Autosomal dominant C1 INH deficiency or dysfunction
Swelling without urticaria or itch
Laryngeal and bowel wall attacks
Triggers: trauma, dental work, ACE inhibitors worsen

right.title: HAE management
points: C4 low (screen), C1q normal in hereditary
C1 INH concentrate or icatibant on demand
Lanadelumab kallikrein prophylaxis
Androgens historical prophylaxis, tranexamic weaker

steps.tx: **Regulators map** keeps complement self limited: C1 INH at initiation, C4 binding protein and factor I at convertases, factor H guarding surfaces, DAF accelerating decay, MCP cofactoring, CD59 at the pore, each regulator's defect a named disease (factor H atypical HUS and C3 glomerulopathy, CD59 and DAF loss in PNH via PIGA). The cascade is brakes as much as engine.
steps.say: Every activation step has a named brake; brake failure is a disease catalogue.

left.title: Fluid phase brakes
points: C1 inhibitor: initiation
Factor H and I: C3b management on surfaces
C4 binding protein: classical convertase
Carboxypeptidase trims anaphylatoxins

right.title: Membrane brakes
points: DAF (CD55): convertase decay
MCP (CD46): factor I cofactor
CD59: MAC blockade
PNH loses CD55 and CD59 together (GPI anchor)

steps.tx: **PNH** (paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria) unites this module: somatic PIGA mutation strips GPI anchored CD55 and CD59 from a blood stem cell clone, complement lyses its red cells (intravascular haemolysis, dark urine), thrombosis and marrow failure accompany, FLAER flow cytometry diagnoses the anchor loss, and C5 blockade transformed survival. One mutation connects complement, flow cytometry and therapeutics.
steps.say: Lose the anchor, lose both brakes, and complement eats your own red cells at night.

left.title: PNH portrait
points: PIGA mutation, GPI anchor absent
CD55 and CD59 missing on clone cells
Intravascular haemolysis, LDH and haemoglobinuria
Venous thrombosis in unusual sites

right.title: PNH answers
points: FLAER and CD55 CD59 flow diagnosis
Eculizumab, ravulizumab C5 blockade
Meningococcal vaccination mandatory
Marrow failure may need transplantation

steps.tx: **Complement laboratory strategy** sequences economically: CH50 (classical through terminal) and AH50 (alternative) as screens, C3 and C4 levels as consumption patterns (classical both low, alternative C3 low C4 normal), factor assays and genetics where screens point, and functional vigilance during infections that consume faster than synthesis.
steps.say: CH50 absent, AH50 present points classical; both absent points C3 or terminal.

left.title: Pattern reads
points: Low C4 and C3: classical or lectin consumption
Low C3 normal C4: alternative activation
Low CH50 normal AH50: early classical defect
Both zero: C3 or terminal defect

right.title: Assay cautions
points: Complement is labile: sample handling matters
Acute consumption mimics deficiency transiently
Repeat in convalescence before labelling
Genetics for regulator diseases

steps.tx: **Complement in disease mechanisms** recurs across the curriculum: lupus consumption, infection defence, transplant antibody mediated rejection (C4d staining in graft biopsies as classical footprint), atypical HUS dysregulation, and age related macular degeneration factor H genetics. The pathway diagram is a map several specialties share.
steps.say: C4d in a graft is complement's fingerprint at a rejection crime scene.

left.title: Consumption diseases
points: SLE activity follows C3 C4 and anti dsDNA
Post infectious GN: C3 low, recovers in weeks
C3 glomerulopathy: persistent alternative activation
Cryoglobulins consume classical

right.title: Deposition evidence
points: C4d in transplant biopsies: antibody mediated rejection
C1q in lupus full house staining
MAC in infarcted and inflamed tissue
Complement split products as trial biomarkers
